verdicts.reason: Live data-analyst postings (ALO Yoga, Impiricus) require 'Python or R for data analysis' and a Statistics degree, and MIT lists 18.05 as an approved probability/statistics course in the Statistics and Data Science minor.
Aggregated live ML-engineer intern postings explicitly require a 'solid foundation in linear algebra, calculus, and statistics,' which 18.06 (Linear Algebra) directly supplies.
MIT's Statistics and Data Science minor lists 18.600 Probability and Random Variables as one of its required subjects, tying the probability-theory foundation to the statistics track.
Live ML-engineer postings demand a foundation in statistics and the ml-engineer profile names probability as a non-stale foundation, which 18.600's rigorous probability theory provides.
ML-engineer postings require linear-algebra foundations and deep-learning frameworks, and 18.C06 teaches linear algebra plus gradient descent and regularization, the core mechanics of model training.

18.C06 teaches convex optimization and linear/quadratic programming, which are the definitional optimization-modeling methods of operations-research analysis (or-analyst's core skill of formulating mathematical models under constraints).

Data-scientist postings and the SDS minor treat 18.C06 only as a generic interchangeable linear-algebra prerequisite (18.03/18.06/18.C06); its convex-optimization content is not a distinctive data-scientist skill, and the judge itself rated it optimization-focused rather than data-mining.

ML-engineer postings require deep-learning frameworks and a completed ML project, and Databricks' ML intern posting names deep learning/PyTorch; 18.065 covers neural networks, ML fundamentals, and matrix factorizations.

MIT lists 18.065 (Matrix Methods in Data Analysis, Signal Processing and Machine Learning) as an approved course in the Statistics and Data Science minor, and its PCA/dimensionality-reduction content maps to the data-scientist distinctive feature-selection/data-mining skill.
MIT's Statistics minor lists 18.650[J] Fundamentals of Statistics as a required subject, directly delivering the statistician's core estimation, testing, and inference methods.

18.650 is a required subject in the Statistics and Data Science minor and its regression/classification content matches the statistical-modeling asked for in live data/analytics postings ('experience with forecasting and statistical analysis').

MIT's course pages confirm 18.453 Combinatorial Optimization covers linear programming, network flow, matroid optimization, and NP-hard problems, which are the definitional optimization methods of operations-research analysis.
